Existing member details display the saved scope. Local desktop creation dialog and existing Owner readback inspected without granting access; scope/role interaction tests, operator integration tests and dashboard check passed. Invitation delivery, recipient handoff, real permission mutation, translated interaction states and responsive review remain open.
Whole-story countermeasure now specified in docs/product/member-invitation-flow.md on the GitHub handoff branch: separate short-lived purpose-bound invitation from reusable operator session credential; explicit owner scope/role, recipient identity/acceptance, truthful delivery state, expiry/cancel/replacement and durable exactly-once membership receipt. Do not assume profile-email verification, mail delivery or self-registration; current first-access constraint remains related niu-287.5. Uses mature GitHub invitation lifecycle reference. No invitation sent or product implementation changed; existing owner preserved.
title: Member onboarding requires sharing a temporary access token with no sign-in handoff

comments.text: Additional desktop staging evidence 2026-11-03: a revoked key detail’s Spending limit section explicitly says personal API-key routes do not consume this allowance. This clarifies the distinction after creation, but the create-key form does not show that explanation at the moment the user chooses a cap. Actual enforcement remains untested; ensure consistent wording at creation and detail.

description: On 2026-11-03 in the signed-in Chinese staging workspace at desktop width, Create API key > optional limits describes the dollar cap as this key’s cumulative spending allowance and says blank means unlimited. The workspace model catalog separately describes its routes as upstream-funded and paid directly by the owning account. The form does not say whether the cap covers those upstream charges, leaving a user unable to judge whether the control limits their actual expense. Local documentation states key spending limits apply to customer-liability reservations; the deployed revision and actual enforcement for these routes were not verified. No key or charge was created. See docs/ux/staging-review-2026-11-02.md.
notes:
Added customer-charge versus direct Provider billing explanation at key creation and currency-limit editing, with Chinese translation. Key integration tests and new i18n audit pass. Still requires running the actual UI and validating deployed customer-priced and upstream-funded enforcement, including zero, finite and unlimited behavior; do not close yet.
Local desktop browser confirmed customer-versus-Provider charge explanation is visible at creation with the optional limit expanded. Actual charge enforcement and zero, finite and unlimited behavior remain unverified.
title: Explain what an API key spending limit does and does not cover

acceptance_criteria: Localize key-detail statuses, restriction labels, usage figures and associated history control names consistently in Chinese, retaining correct units and unknown/unlimited semantics. Verify inactive and active keys, history menus and English locale without exposing internal identifiers.
description: On 2026-11-03, a revoked key detail in the Chinese staging interface mixes Chinese explanatory text with English operational labels: Requests per minute, Concurrent requests, Tokens per minute, Allow all sources, Lifetime limit, Committed, Remaining allowance and No recorded requests. The history menu names inherit English metric labels. This affects understanding of key restrictions and historical use. Observed at desktop for one inactive key; active keys, other locales, editing and actual screen-reader speech were not tested. See docs/ux/staging-review-2026-11-02.md.
title: Localize API key details and limit history labels in Chinese

acceptance_criteria: Show localized media-type choices and selected states in the Chinese interface, preserve their filter values and verify open, selected and empty-result states plus English locale. Keep keyboard semantics and focus behavior.
description: On 2026-11-03 in the Chinese staging workspace Assets page at 1440 × 900, opening the 全部媒体 filter shows All media, Images, Videos and Audio in English. Choosing Images changes the closed trigger to 图片 and the empty result remains available. The mixed-language menu makes selection less predictable for Chinese readers. The library was empty; populated results and other locales were not tested. No file was uploaded. See docs/ux/staging-review-2026-11-02.md.
title: Localize media-type filter choices in Chinese

acceptance_criteria: For unresolved or inaccessible key links, explain that the key cannot be found or accessed in the current workspace without asserting an unverified cause or disclosing cross-workspace existence; provide a scoped return to the key list. Verify nonexistent, deleted, unauthorized and temporarily unavailable cases against actual backend responses and preserve safe authorization boundaries.
description: On 2026-11-03, an authenticated staging user opened a deliberately nonexistent key slug within the Default workspace. The page says 此密钥不属于所选工作空间 (this key does not belong to the selected workspace) and offers Return to API keys. The recovery link is useful, but the diagnosis asserts a workspace mismatch for an arbitrary nonexistent link and may prompt users to look in the wrong workspace. Other causes, permission denials and deleted keys were not tested. No data was changed. See docs/ux/staging-review-2026-11-02.md.
notes:
Replaced unsupported workspace-mismatch assertion with neutral not-found-or-inaccessible language and retained scoped return link; added regression coverage for absent keys and preserved read-failure handling. Browser and authorization-path verification remain outstanding.
Local desktop browser confirmed nonexistent key displays neutral message and scoped return link. Deleted, unauthorized and temporarily unavailable backend paths remain to verify; issue stays open.
title: Use a neutral recovery message for an unavailable API key link

acceptance_criteria: Make public catalog and docs directly discoverable from signed-out login at desktop and narrow widths using the existing public navigation conventions, preserving keyboard access, language controls and the login task. Verify the rendered local change and the deployed staging revision at desktop, 390px and narrower widths, including open language menu and keyboard focus. Keep sign-in and account recovery verification separate.
description: 2026-11-02 staging /login in independent signed-out browser: desktop accessibility tree exposes public Models and Docs links; at 390x844 screenshot and accessibility tree these disappear, leaving only home logo and Language. Visitors must infer that the logo leads elsewhere before discovering models or help. Repository ownership explicitly requires direct public catalog/docs links on login. No sign-in submitted.
notes:
Removed mobile-only rule hiding Models and Docs, reduced mobile header spacing. Browser verification remains pending: local development startup dependencies and browser connection timed out; do not close until rendered desktop, 390px and narrower navigation and language menu are inspected.
2026-11-03: local React Router/Vite process started, but browser navigation timed out. Direct local /login returned HTTP 500 reporting a 60-second Vite transport invoke timeout for the server manifest. Host was heavily loaded; no rendered layout evidence. Pending browser verification remains.
2026-11-03: local frontend rendered desktop login with Models, Docs and language control; test backend was unavailable and login correctly reported unavailable, so sign-in behavior was not tested. IAB viewport override did not change the target tab screenshot from desktop size. Narrow, language menu and keyboard verification remain outstanding.
2026-11-03 review reconciliation: reopened because the local rendered fix is not evidence of a deployed staging correction. The issue originated in staging and carries needs-verification; verify the affected login navigation against the deployed revision at desktop and narrow widths before closing. Authentication and other login recovery remain separate.
2026-11-03 staging recheck in signed-out in-app browser at 390×844, Chinese locale: Models and Docs are still absent from the visible header and accessibility tree, while desktop state before resizing exposed both. The local fix is not reflected in this observed deployment. No sign-in attempted; deployed revision unknown.
title: Narrow sign-in hides the direct public Models and Docs links

acceptance_criteria: Present localized role names, authority explanations, scope qualifiers and known access-activity event labels in Chinese; preserve actual user-entered names and event semantics. Show a truthful understandable fallback for unknown event types. Verify owner, admin and viewer cases, historical events and English locale without modifying access.
description: On 2026-11-03, the Chinese organization Members page shows the owner role in Chinese, but opening the member detail displays Owner, the scope phrase all workspaces, and the explanation of the role’s ability to change data, add users and revoke access in English. The recent activity list also mixes English password login succeeded with Chinese session-revoked events. These are the details an organization administrator needs to understand authority and access history. Observed for one owner account at 1440 × 900; other roles and event types were not tested. No access was changed. See docs/ux/staging-review-2026-11-02.md.
title: Localize member role and access activity in Chinese

acceptance_criteria: Verify the actual semantics and clearly explain each model and Provider mode, including inheritance/intersection with existing key grants, empty selection, future additions and block-all impact where applicable. Localize choices in Chinese, retain explicit uncertainty when data is missing, and verify selection, review, discard and authorized enforcement without exposing confidential data.
description: On 2026-11-03 in the Chinese workspace Guardrails > Policy > Model access page at desktop width, the model restriction menu offers No additional restriction, Allow all, Allow selected and Block all in English, without explaining how the first two differ or how each interacts with key grants. Choosing Allow selected shows a clear warning that zero selected models blocks all requests; selecting one shows its name. A workspace administrator cannot compare the other modes confidently before changing a policy. The choices were tested only in unsaved state and discarded; actual enforcement and other roles were not tested. See docs/ux/staging-review-2026-11-02.md.
title: Explain model and Provider access modes before selection

acceptance_criteria: Determine actual Provider eligibility and authority for this workspace, distinguish genuinely empty, unavailable and unauthorized states without leaking platform data, and offer a role-appropriate next step. Preserve the warning and prevent accidental adoption of an empty allowlist through clear review. Verify populated, empty, denied and failed loading states and actual enforcement in an isolated test.
description: On 2026-11-03 in the signed-in Chinese Default workspace at desktop width, Guardrails > Policy > Model access > Provider restriction > Allow selected warns that selecting none blocks all inference, but its picker says no Provider has been configured and offers no selection or remedy. The same workspace catalog lists upstream-funded model routes; this does not establish that their Providers should be visible or selectable in this policy. The user cannot tell whether configuration, authorization, filtering or loading prevents selection. The restriction was not saved. See docs/ux/staging-review-2026-11-02.md.
title: Make an empty Provider restriction picker actionable and trustworthy

acceptance_criteria: At candidate selection and review, provide trustworthy, authorized model capability, availability and customer-facing cost context, including explicit unknowns and a scoped path to details. Do not imply a catalog entry proves support or admission and do not expose Provider procurement data. Verify create/edit, unsupported and unknown states and preservation of existing policy semantics.
description: On 2026-11-03 in the Chinese staging Default workspace, editing an existing custom routing model presents a candidate picker containing only five model names. The catalog for the same workspace marks their capabilities unpublished and upstream-funded; the picker does not show those qualifications, cost availability or a route to inspect them. The form invites visual, tool and structured-output routing rules, so a user cannot judge whether a candidate fits or is available from the decision point. One disabled saved policy was inspected without changing or saving it; actual availability, eligibility and other deployment datasets remain unverified. See docs/ux/staging-review-2026-11-02.md.
title: Provide decision context when choosing routing candidates

acceptance_criteria: Determine the actual EPay integration requirements and provide deployment-correct callback defaults or clear, secure instructions and validation where operator input is necessary. Explain required merchant information and verification/readiness separately from saved configuration. Verify incomplete, invalid, configured and failure-recovery states in an isolated environment without exposing credentials or performing real payments.
description: On 2026-11-03 in the Chinese desktop staging administrator view, Payments > EPay setup asks for merchant ID, gateway URL, notification URL, return URL, secret and enabled methods in one dialog. It offers no visible explanation, example, generated value or verification guidance for the two callback URLs or where to obtain the gateway details. An operator must infer deployment-specific integration details before enabling customer top-ups. No fields were filled or saved; actual validation, payment-provider requirements and checkout were not tested. See docs/ux/staging-review-2026-11-02.md.
title: Guide administrators through EPay setup and callback URLs

acceptance_criteria: Keep organization context and switching discoverable while consolidating low-frequency organization actions. Verify single and multiple organizations, permissions, switching, creation, settings, errors and keyboard interaction using the rendered desktop menu; retain existing user capabilities.
description: Desktop staging account menu gives multiple primary rows to organization selection, creation and management even though administration is infrequent; this crowds everyday account actions. Preserve visible current organization and discoverable switching and self-service administration.
notes:
An initial nested-menu attempt regressed organization switching and settings navigation in integration tests and was reverted. The issue remains open; preserve the existing working menu until a replacement passes those flows and rendered interaction review. OpenRouter reference could not be loaded in the browser.
Account menu retains current organization and switching; creation is now reached through Manage organizations and the organization page, reducing one primary menu action. On local desktop, verified menu rendering, organization settings link and opening/cancelling creation dialog. Organization integration and permission tests passed (12 tests), including multiple-organization switching and self-service creation using fixtures. Actual multi-organization and keyboard browser verification remains; responsive review deferred per user.
title: Reduce organization management prominence in account menu

acceptance_criteria: Reproduce under controlled theme and locale settings, determine whether production is affected, and ensure server and client initial attributes agree without losing saved appearance or locale; verify both initial rendering and subsequent changes.
description: Local dashboard development server logged a React hydration mismatch on the root html element: server and client differed in theme class, data-locale and color-scheme attributes during signed-in About inspection. User-visible impact and production behavior have not been established.
title: Investigate dashboard hydration mismatch for theme and locale

acceptance_criteria: Keep the editable composer and controls visually cohesive while showing relevant billing and key-recovery information outside its boundary; preserve readable attribution, focus, error recovery and transcript clearance. Verify real desktop interaction and long/unknown billing states; defer broader responsive review per user.
description: User reports that informational copy inside Chat composer disrupts its layout. Local signed-in Chat shows billing explanation below the composer controls inside the bordered input surface; key-recovery messaging uses the same surface.
notes:
Moved billing and key-recovery notices below the bordered composer. Local signed-in desktop screenshot shows the input surface and notice separately; focused billing regression test passed, including mixed and manual-key wording. Long/unknown billing and keyboard checks remain; narrow layouts are deferred per user.
Local desktop checked Chat settings open and Escape closes it with focus returning to the settings control. Mixed/manual billing unit regression passed; only own-key billing was visually inspected. Long/unknown states and other view widths remain unverified.
2026-11-04: Following real catalog-to-Chat handoff, desktop 1280x720 screenshot exposed first-run cards behind the floating composer and billing text. Changed Generations Chat to separate scrollable transcript and composer grid rows, removing dynamic overlay padding. Local desktop inspected first run, scroll to final examples, saved conversation, and billing notice outside the input; 102 ModelTable/Playground integration tests and dashboard type check passed. Long and unknown notices, intermediate widths, later responsive review, and deployed behavior remain to verify.
title: Move Chat billing and key notices outside composer surface

acceptance_criteria: Display detailed text and media selling schedules as a labeled table, preserve rates, units, missing values, context tiers and historical rounding semantics; avoid nested tables in compact list rows. Verify history and promotion views in the rendered desktop UI and appropriate tests, with responsive follow-up deferred as requested.
description: Price history and promotion details render rates as unaligned prose, making categories, units and amounts difficult to compare. User requested a table while inspecting local pricing history on 2026-11-04. OpenRouter model detail displays comparable input, output and cache prices in aligned table columns; compact price summaries already sit inside a parent table.
notes: 2026-11-04: Detailed text/media schedules now use shared shadcn table primitives, with context tier groups and unchanged amounts, units, missing-rate and rounding semantics. Compact summaries stay as text inside their existing parent table. Compared OpenRouter model page pricing columns. At 1280×720 in an isolated local deployment, checked text history and a synthetic promotion original/result comparison; adjusted excessive row padding after screenshot. Three component tests cover text tiers, media terms and compact non-nesting. Media/tier rendered views and deferred responsive pass remain unverified.
title: Present detailed selling prices as a readable table

acceptance_criteria: Keep the dialog frame and both rounded corners visually intact with long scrollable content, retain a visible usable scrollbar and keyboard scrolling, and verify multiple long and short dialogs in the browser. Record responsive follow-up separately per product owner.
description: On the locally rendered long pricing dialogs at desktop width, the native scrollbar track extends across the rounded dialog edge, visibly cutting through the corner and border. The same DialogContent primitive is shared by other long dialogs.
title: Keep scrollbars inside rounded dialog edges

acceptance_criteria: Across login, public docs and navigation, visible locale, document language/title and accessible language trigger accurately reflect the active selection after navigation, reload and language switch. Verify selected menu state, keyboard, screen reader naming, desktop and narrow layouts in English and Simplified Chinese.
description: 2026-11-03 staging /docs/ in an independent signed-out browser after choosing Simplified Chinese on login: documentation text and selector label display Chinese, and the open radio menu marks Simplified Chinese selected, but the language trigger accessibility Help reports Language: English and page title remains English. This produces contradictory language state for users and assistive technology. No settings or account data were changed; browser preference only.
title: Documentation language control reports English while Chinese is selected

acceptance_criteria: Keep the active underline visible without a vertical scrollbar when the tabs fit; retain horizontal access, keyboard navigation and active-tab visibility when space is constrained. Verify on the rendered Provider pages and record responsive follow-up separately.
description: At desktop width, the Provider section tabs display a vertical scrollbar beside a single row. The horizontal overflow wrapper also becomes vertically scrollable, while the active underline extends below the tab list.
title: Remove unintended vertical scrollbar from Provider section tabs

acceptance_criteria: For hosted staging and other explicitly selected deployments, the copied setup workflow communicates the intended origin and makes its scope visible during authorization without exposing secrets or silently switching environments; normal production and self-hosted paths remain correct. Verify prompt, agent handoff and origin readback with current deployment capabilities; do not claim connection from documentation alone.
description: 2026-11-03 signed-out staging: homepage and Build with Niu give a setup prompt that says only to follow the canonical niu.io installation document. The linked installation guide says hosted Niu is default and a non-default origin must be the deployment selected by the user. The prompt copied from staging contains no staging origin, so an agent following the documented default may connect a different environment. This is a reasoned risk from the prompt and guide; no agent installation or authorization was performed. Canonical documentation links can remain canonical.
design: 2026-11-04 review and countermeasure: actual niu-login rejects the selected /niu/ deployment before authorization. Carry a validated optional deployment mount through device endpoints, browser verification, private version-1 credentials, connection checks and MCP gateway selection; legacy origin-only credentials stay valid. Restrict mount segments, preserve same-origin and explicit gateway matching, refuse redirects and credentials/query/fragment. Verify an actual isolated mounted login and resulting credential/MCP readback, plus root compatibility and malicious path rejection; deployment and retained browser session remain separate verification scopes.
notes:
2026-11-03 staging Event subscriptions empty state offers Copy agent prompt. Local source agent-review/page.tsx uses an absolute production https://niu.io/docs/agents.md in this prompt for routing, evaluations and events; this is source evidence for an additional consumer, not proof of the deployed clipboard contents. Ensure the selected staging/local origin and workspace remain unambiguous in all these prompts and verify copied text in the browser.
Docs home now displays and copies the current browser origin; Build with Niu points to that deployment-specific prompt. Dashboard routing/evaluations/events prompts now include origin and human-readable workspace URL and request authorization readback. Docs build and nine agent-review tests passed, including clipboard content in a fixture. Local browser displayed the correct docs origin and both copy actions showed success; browser clipboard readback was unavailable. Public website homepage is in another repository, deployed staging/production/self-hosted authorization and actual agent handoff remain unverified.
2026-11-04: actual niu-login rejected the explicitly selected /niu/ URL before network access. Implemented source-build mount propagation across device authorization, saved version-1 credential and MCP; origin-only credentials remain compatible and configured base mismatch is rejected. Isolated local current-source package and real browser authorized Default with invocation disabled; mounted /v1/key and /v1/models returned 200, packaged MCP inspect_key read invocation disabled, credential file mode 0600, mismatch and unsafe URL samples rejected. The issued isolated key was revoked and its subsequent request returned 401. Actual routing-page copy action included mount and workspace; narrow rendered page inspected. This is development evidence, not a hosted release, installed host integration, staging verification, or proof that all setup prompt surfaces carry a mount. Keep open.
Independent source-level verification at GitHub402cad347520abab5e8dd41fca7b795a6b43a836: deployment parser accepts root HTTPS, mounted HTTPS and mounted loopback HTTP; rejects traversal, encoded/double-slash paths, query, fragment, credentials, insecure nonloopback HTTP and backslash paths (3 positive and8 negative cases). Disposable synthetic credential roundtrip verifies old root schema and mounted schema, mode0600, exact MCP /v1 base, payload logging defaultfalse, conflicting explicit gateway rejection and nonprivate-file denial. No real credential/network request used; temporary files removed. Does not certify packaged host installation or real browser authorization.
title: Staging agent setup prompt omits the selected deployment

acceptance_criteria: Render and expose consistent, correctly localized public catalog titles, field/button names and landmarks in both supported locales, including first load and after language switching. Verify screen-reader labels and keyboard interaction at desktop and narrow widths; retain Niu brand spelling and model names.
description: 2026-11-03 signed-out staging /models/ with Simplified Chinese selected: after page settles, visible catalog heading and empty state are Chinese, but accessibility tree still names search Filter models, refresh Refresh, the Published models region, home Niu home and Footer navigation in English. Initial page also displayed English before switching to Chinese. This concerns public catalog control/landmark localization, distinct from dashboard issue niu-lxs.31; no model records or preferences changed beyond browser locale.
title: Chinese public model catalog leaves control names and footer landmarks in English

acceptance_criteria:
1. Remove the personal browser-local 'Interface language' control from the deployment-wide Admin Branding form (keep personal language in AccountMenu).
2. Add visual color swatches/pickers alongside the 8 theme color hex inputs.
description:
Trigger: Opening '/admin/branding?tab=theme'.
Impact: branding/page.tsx:120-135 places the personal browser-local 'Interface language' selector inside the deployment-wide Admin Branding '<form onSubmit={save}>', misleading admins into thinking they are setting the installation-wide default language (and wondering why 'Discard changes' / 'Reset to Niu defaults' does not affect it). Below it, 'Colors' (line 129) renders 8 raw hex text inputs ('#rrggbb') with no color swatches or color pickers.
Source: apps/dashboard/app/features/branding/page.tsx:120-135.

acceptance_criteria:
1. Render the breadcrumb current page title in ShellHeader as plain text rather than a duplicate navigation dropdown.
2. Align ShellHeader and child route headers so pages do not render stacked duplicate or contradictory headings.
description:
Trigger: Viewing any workspace route in the dashboard shell.
Impact: ShellHeader.tsx:287-316 wraps the breadcrumb <h1> route title inside a <DropdownMenuTrigger> button ('Switch workspace page') with <ChevronsUpDown>, creating two adjacent lookalike dropdown triggers in the top bar that duplicate the left workspace sidebar. Below ShellHeader, child routes (organization/page.tsx:78, WorkspaceDirectory.tsx:26, OperatorsView.tsx:413, billing/page.tsx:281, models/page.tsx:38) render a second <PageHeader> with mismatched titles (e.g. 'Billing' above 'Usage statements', 'Organization' above 'Organization settings').
Source: apps/dashboard/app/shell/ShellHeader.tsx:287-316,360-380; apps/dashboard/app/features/billing/page.tsx:281; apps/dashboard/app/features/organization/page.tsx:78.
notes: 2026-11-03 staging reproduction: from Organization settings > Users for Default, the workspace page heading is Users, but opening its page-switcher lists no Users item and marks Settings as selected. This misleading current-page indication is observed independently of whether Settings is its intended parent. No navigation was selected.
title: Remove duplicate page-switcher dropdown on breadcrumb H1 title and eliminate stacked duplicate PageHeaders

acceptance_criteria: Deliver an inline before/after preview and explain the color correction and any verification limits.
close_reason: Delivered additional large and compact typography-direction preview: rounded monospaced Latin with YouYuan-style Chinese. This is generated concept art, not exact named-font rendering or production browser verification. No product assets changed.
description: User screenshot shows the top brown and upper-right burnt-orange logo blades disappearing against a dark header. Inspect canonical artwork and produce a non-destructive palette comparison preserving the six-blade shape and Niu wordmark. Scope is palette exploration; production assets remain unchanged.
notes:
Inspected canonical raster and supplied dark-header screenshot. Delivered generated warm amber/orange/coral palette preview with raised luminance of top and upper-right blades. Preview is directional artwork, not a pixel-exact production recolor; no source assets or UI changed. Production size and browser validation remain outside this palette-preview scope.
Follow-up request extends the preview to softly rounded monospaced English and YouYuan-style Chinese typography. Produce large and compact directional specimens; exact font rendering and production asset integration are not yet claimed.

acceptance_criteria:
1. Provide built-in video model presets (e.g. Seedance, Kling, Veo, Sora, Generic Video) that pre-populate byte limits, MIME types, and pixel dimension mappings automatically.
2. Present simple checkboxes for supported input modalities, resolutions, aspect ratios, and durations by default, keeping raw schema overrides collapsed under an optional advanced section.

Trigger: Clicking 'Configure video' / 'Edit video configuration' inside ModelMappingForm on '/admin/providers/:providerId/keys' or '/models'.
Impact: VideoSchemaEditor.tsx:25-193 forces admins to manually fill 5 tabs ('General', 'Inputs', 'Controls', 'Output', 'Rules') with raw adapter channel names, max request bytes ('16777216'), comma-separated MIME strings ('image/png, image/jpeg'), 9 low-level control min/max/byte bounds, manual 'Width (px)' x 'Height (px)' pixel estimation tables for every resolution x aspect ratio pair, and comma-separated incompatible control pairs.
Source: apps/dashboard/app/features/providers/components/VideoSchemaEditor.tsx:25-193; apps/dashboard/app/features/providers/video-schema.ts:1-40; apps/dashboard/app/features/providers/components/ModelMappingForm.tsx:160-178.
title: Replace 5-tab raw byte/MIME/pixel VideoSchemaEditor with built-in video model presets and simple capability toggles

acceptance_criteria: Actual hosted browser enables/disables plugin; success and duplicate notifications credit exactly once; failed checkout gives no credit; reload/restart preserves state. Independently verify final order and balance artifacts, with desktop/narrow UI inspection. Fixture results provide no evidence.
close_reason: Hosted activation, signed settlement, duplicate idempotency, non-crediting unpaid paths, durable restart state and responsive UI verified with current-input production flows and independent final artifacts. Terminal unpaid browser recovery is separately captured in niu-0gj.
description: Existing niu#99 local-only policy is superseded by explicit user authorization for online use. Package the simulated merchant as a public plugin; keep authoritative accounting in core and composition in cloud. Support release builds, same-origin checkout and durable merchant state, with user-controlled activation.
notes:
Implemented public built-in merchant plugin, release-mode support, bounded same-origin checkout proxy, PostgreSQL merchant persistence, and persistent simulated top-up labels. Local current-input browser run created USD 1.23 top-up, restarted both processes, selected duplicate confirmation; independent PostgreSQL reads found two accepted deliveries, exactly one settlement and one matching balance entry. Release compilation and dashboard builds completed. Hosted acceptance remains pending; no fixture outcomes used.
Published immutable core release v0.2.25 (8d44fe86); cloud composition 9a4aaf8 triggers hosted deployment. Local declined-payment run produced no additional ledger entry; disabling preserves paid simulated=true in the independently read order API. Public controls returned 404 and cross-origin mutation returned 403. Desktop and 390px checkout inspected including open menu; UI width equals viewport. Hosted verification remains pending.
Hosted v0.2.25 is live (cloud 9a4aaf8). Actual demo browser enabled the previously unavailable plugin, created a top-up and selected duplicate notifications. Two accepted deliveries produced exactly one matching balance transaction. Fresh API checkout runs exercised success/failure/cancel/timeout/out-of-order/delayed scenarios; independent final order, transaction and balance APIs found four successful scenarios credited once each, no unpaid credits, exact aggregate delta and unchanged other-currency balances. Render restart produced a new merchant startup; disabled selection and all orders persisted, delayed confirmation settled. Browser re-enabled plugin for authorized ongoing audit. Desktop and 390px configuration/checkout inspected. Existing terminal unpaid recovery limitation is separately tracked in niu-0gj / niu#114. No upstream inference calls or real payments were made.
title: Ship user-selectable hosted mock payment plugin

close_reason: Implemented and verified in unit/integration suites (261 tests passing, 0 check-i18n findings) and live browser inspection on 127.0.0.1:2566 across desktop (1440x900) and mobile (390x844).
description: Trigger: Top-down Workspace IA and video-asset design review on 2026-11-02 (docs/ux/workspace-and-ux-review-2026-11-02.md). title: Consolidate Workspace IA into 6 sections (move Members to Org SettingsDialog, unify Library + Video setup into Assets, merge Activity into Overview)

description: Trigger: apps/gateway/src/request_payloads.rs:132 defaults payload capture to true; capture() buffers up to 1 MiB of request bytes (142-190) and tees the response stream into another 1 MiB buffer, then writes to storage through a global semaphore of 4 (request_payloads.rs:15). request_timings.rs:104-150 writes a timing row per attempt through another semaphore of 4. description:
Trigger: Clicking 'New workspace' in WorkspaceSwitcher or 'Create organization' in AccountMenu.
Impact: Create Workspace renders '<Input id="workspace-reset" value="Never (lifetime)" readOnly />' (WorkspaceSwitcher.tsx:148)—an uneditable text input exposing a database constraint. Both modals force users to deal with a top-level regex-validated 'Slug' field ('Used in ?org=<slug>...'), and Create Organization asks for 'Initial workspace (optional)' while regenerating crypto.randomUUID() on every keystroke (lines 238, 259).
Source: apps/dashboard/app/shell/WorkspaceSwitcher.tsx:39-47,83-291.
notes:
2026-11-03 staging revalidation: Create organization auto-filled example-studio after entering Example Studio, so users need not manually supply a slug in this normal case. The Slug field, ?org= query syntax and character rules nevertheless occupy primary form space and require unnecessary technical knowledge; initial workspace defaults to Default. No creation was submitted. Revalidate workspace behavior and current source independently before implementing.
2026-11-03 staging: Create workspace shows read-only Reset = Never (lifetime), and typing Example Studio auto-fills example-studio. The Slug still occupies a top-level field with route syntax; no workspace was created. This confirms existing evidence while correcting any inference that the slug must normally be typed manually.
2026-11-03 Chinese mobile staging: a synthetic Chinese organization name suggested lowercase pinyin, and a manually edited slug remained unchanged after editing the name. Entering an invalid mixed-case slug containing a space and punctuation left Create organization enabled and only the general character rules visible; no submit was attempted, so validation or normalization at submission is unverified. Dialog was cancelled.
title: Simplify Create Workspace and Create Organization modals by removing read-only Reset Period and mandatory Slug fields

acceptance_criteria:
1. Load all configured provider models without '.slice(0, 12)' truncation.
2. Keep the editor modal open on network timeout so user edits are never lost.
3. Remove internal 'Revision X' labels from the table, editor header, and save notice.
description:
Trigger: Creating or editing a platform route pool on '/admin/routing'.
Impact: (1) route-pools/page.tsx:677 ('providerResult.data.slice(0, 12)') only fetches models from the first 12 provider API key connections, silently hiding models on the 13th+ connection. (2) On network timeout ('writeMayHaveCommitted'), lines 580-583 and 947-955 call 'setEditing(null)', destroying the open editor modal and wiping all unsaved work. (3) Lines 878-888 and 1533-1578 require every conditional rule target candidate to also belong to the top-level pool candidates list. (4) 'Revision X' is displayed in the table cell (line 396), dialog header (line 1014), save notice (line 942), and history modal (line 2256).
Source: apps/dashboard/app/features/route-pools/page.tsx:396,580-583,677,878-900,942-955,1014,1531-1608,2256.
notes:
2026-11-04 partial: Candidate discovery now traverses every configured Provider in batches of 12, with a regression covering the 13th. Uncertain pool writes keep the editor and its draft visible, disable another save and explain how to check the saved list; do not close this issue: a draft-preserving reconciliation flow, duplicate candidate requirements, revision presentation, failed discovery, desktop error-state and responsive verification remain. Local desktop editor and candidate menu inspected with two synthetic Providers; route-pools suite passes (4 tests).
Removed revision numbers from pool list, editor, save confirmation and history entries; recorded dates and states remain visible. Numeric revision remains in the concurrency contract. Reconciliation and visual verification remain incomplete.
Added routing discovery and uncertain-write acceptance branches to docs/ux/staging-acceptance-test-requirements.md. Dashboard type check and i18n audit pass.
The editor also warns when Provider discovery is incomplete instead of silently presenting a partial list; retry currently requires reopening the editor. This recovery and its rendered error state still need improvement and verification.
2026-11-04: Failed Provider discovery now has an in-place retry that retains the route draft; regression covers failure followed by successful rediscovery. Route-pools suite passes (5 tests). Browser verification of the failure and retry remains outstanding. Confirmed storage serializes writes per alias and checks expected revision; the uncertain-write reconciliation must respect this concurrency boundary.
Revalidated the conditional-rule duplication finding: storage validation explicitly requires every rule candidate alias to belong to the pool candidate set (crates/storage/src/route_pools.rs, validate_pool_candidates_and_rules), and admission validates those pool aliases. Removing only the UI constraint would yield rejected saves; a proper fix needs a product decision on rule/default candidate semantics plus matching storage, authorization, dispatch, contracts and tests. Do not silently remove this check.
Added in-editor saved-state check after uncertain writes and revision conflicts. Unchanged state permits a revision-guarded retry while preserving the draft; failed reads remain retryable and changed saved state blocks overwrites. Automated coverage exercises failed read, missing pool, guarded retry and a concurrent change (5 route-pool tests pass). Still incomplete: present and reconcile the changed saved configuration alongside the draft, actual browser error-state verification, and rule-candidate semantics across backend and runtime.
Saved-state check now recognizes when the authoritative configuration matches the interrupted write, adopts that revision without overwriting it, and preserves any edits made since submission. Regression includes a synthetic committed write with a lost response (6 route-pool tests pass). Divergent concurrent state still needs an in-editor comparison/reconciliation; no completion claimed.
2026-11-04: Divergent saved route settings are now displayed in the retained editor alongside the draft, including scope, billing, candidates and rule conditions. Explicitly continuing with the draft adopts the saved revision but does not write until Save; regression verifies the ensuing payload uses that revision. Different ownership/project scope cannot be overwritten. Six route-pool tests, dashboard type check and i18n audit pass. Browser verification of conflict/error states and semantics of conditional rule candidates remain outstanding; keep open.
Local isolated resale gateway, 1280×720 desktop: created a synthetic priced mapping and existing pool, submitted a different same-alias draft, observed conflict and preserved inputs, checked saved state, verified saved details and focus, chose Continue with my draft, saved and observed the resulting draft name on the list. No real upstream or paid request. Adjusted recovery focus and message placement after screenshot revealed the long dialog concealed the comparison. Error discovery retry, lost-response browser branch, other roles and deferred responsive remain unverified; rule-candidate semantics remain separate work.
After checking an uncertain create, retain alias and scope lock until a definitive resolution: an earlier in-flight request could otherwise commit under the old alias while an edited alias creates another pool. The guarded retry regression verifies both controls stay locked. Desktop synthetic conflict recovery passed end-to-end; responsive and lost-response browser verification remain pending.
title: Fix /admin/routing 12-provider discovery truncation, modal destruction on timeout, duplicate rule candidates, and 'Revision X' leakage

**P2 · decision semantics · G3–G4, J3/J5 · high confidence in UI/source mismatch.**

The Chat model picker labels its first category Popular. Its caller ranks by at most 100 workspace request records and otherwise uses a fixed familiar-family ordering, including when history is absent or loading fails. The picker always labels its first eight usable models Popular; it receives no basis/availability indicator. Evidence: E17; `apps/dashboard/src/app/useModelPopularity.ts`, `features/playground/page.tsx`, and `features/playground/components/PlaygroundView.tsx`.

The finding is not that the ranking is completely fabricated or that defaults are undesirable. Recent workspace usage exists as one signal. The problem is undisclosed scope and fallback: an unmeasured default is presented with the same label as observed use.

Proposed direction: distinguish recent workspace usage from default suggestions and unavailable evidence. Do not invent global popularity or benchmark quality. Keep a useful picker when analytics is absent.

Verification: populated history, zero history and failed history retrieval produce honest category meaning. The scope/window are understandable where useful; a request failure must not make a default look like a measured recommendation.

Proposed direction: retain and interpret supported finish reasons through live and saved results, separating transport termination, content outcome and unknown evidence. Explain a relevant next step without automatic paid retries or promises that increasing a limit will resolve every case.

In Model access, changing the unsaved model restriction to Block all enables Save. Proposed direction: make the commit boundary understandable. Either use explicitly section-scoped drafts and saves, or present a whole-policy editing model with a reviewable pending-change summary and discard path at its save point. Preserve atomic policy validation and revision conflict handling; do not assume separate API writes are required.

**P2 · consequential selection and historical diagnosis · G6, J7 · live history evidence plus assignment-renderer source; no restore or assignment executed.**

An existing blocked-request record references a key policy version containing an external input check. Opening that saved version through Guardrails History shows only “1 required check · matches and unavailable services block requests”, alongside Restore this version. It does not identify the detector or recipient. `History.tsx` types these bindings as `unknown[]` and renders only their count. The key-policy assignment preview in `KeyGuardrails.tsx` uses the same count-only presentation. It includes an Inspect saved rules link to History, but that destination also omits the check identity. Evidence: E35, live version dialog and source.

Impact: the operator cannot distinguish which external check is implicated in the historical block or which check a restore/assignment would require. A count is insufficient identification at a consequential choice. This is not evidence that restoration bypasses backend validation or consent; no restoration or external processing occurred. The historical input-rule version, by contrast, explicitly names its email-address blocking rule.

Proposed direction: identify the saved check and expose the processing information relevant to the decision. Distinguish historical binding from current configuration/availability; when details are no longer resolvable, say so rather than substituting present-day terms as historical fact. Preserve backend validation and applicable consent. The UI need not display internal fingerprints or raw identifiers.

Verification: distinguish two saved policies with equal check counts but different recipients/configurations; inspect available, changed and unavailable bindings before restore or assignment. Confirm the selected policy scope and actual current eligibility in an authorized fixture separately. NN/g visibility, recognition and error-prevention criteria support reviewable consequences; they do not require a separate confirmation for every policy operation.

Imported disposition: New: uncertain key mutation lacks reconciliation and safe recovery

Recheck current code/rendering before implementing; migration is not a new reproduction or authorization for product changes.

**P1 · state/recovery · isolated frontend probes + backend source.** A network rejection leaves an error and re-enables Create/Rotate without checking saved state or warning that the operation may have committed. The backend issues/rotates before constructing the complete response. After response loss, a create retry can create a second credential; a successful rotation may have already invalidated the old secret while the user never received the new one. These consequences are inferred from the implementation path; they were not induced on real keys.

Criterion: distinguish unknown outcome from confirmed failure, prevent harmful retries, and offer a usable recovery path. An intentionally one-time secret is valid; pretending it can always be recovered is not a correction.

Proposed correction: reconcile operation outcome using a suitable request identity/status contract or an equally safe supported flow. Explain the uncertain credential state and direct the owner through explicit recovery. Preserve secret non-retrievability and prevent accidental duplicate issuance. Compare TopupFunding's existing uncertain-result handling rather than designing a generic retry loop.

Acceptance: test response loss both before and after commit, server error after commit, navigation/re-entry and role loss. description: Trigger: When opening Assets (Provider materials / Real-person verification) or Volcengine native tools, useMaterials probes capabilities across all active workspace API keys. If any key in the workspace has a Source IP access policy (allowed_cidrs) that blocks the current client IP (HTTP 403 key_ip_not_allowed: 'This API key does not allow the request source address'), useMaterials records raw English API error text in discoveryErrors and VolcengineView renders a role='alert' banner ('Some native tool contexts could not be discovered. / 部分原生工具上下文发现失败。 Production Gateway Key: This API key does not allow the request source address') with only a 'Retry discovery' button, even when other workspace keys are usable. Impact: Source IP restriction is normal business policy on a key, not an unexpected discovery exception; presenting it as an unhandled error banner without actionable remedies confuses users and offers no path to switch keys, adjust the key's Source IP access policy, or create a key. **P1 · actor handoff · G3, J3 · high confidence in inspected entry points; end-to-end provisioning unverified.**

Observation: the account menu switches existing organizations; Organization settings creates workspaces; Users adds a person with a temporary access token; Account balances manages existing companies. None of these inspected entries exposes company creation or a provisioning guide. `docs/reference/company-creation.md` documents the administrator-only company-creation API. A dashboard source search found no `createCompany` consumer. Evidence: E03–E04 and E11.

Impact: an operator onboarding a new independently funded customer must leave the dashboard and already know the company API. Creating another workspace in the current company is materially different because funds are shared.

Proposed direction: explicitly choose and document console-managed or API-managed company provisioning. Either needs a discoverable operator path through company, owner access, workspace, funds and first usable model. Do not add public self-signup or email invitations merely to imitate another product; those are separate product decisions.

Verification: a new operator can provision an independently funded customer using the supported path, hand off access and verify scope without using a developer's private instructions. Access creation, sign-in and isolation require separately authorized tests.
design: Console-managed customer provisioning is a separate task from Account balances. Reuse company, workspace, scoped owner and password APIs; no public signup or email invitations. Keep independent company funds and configured platform currency. Company, workspace and identity-only owner creation use atomic durable retry receipts. Identity creation issues no session; replay never restores changed/revoked access. Saved setup remains resumable, with tab retry caches disposable. Password configuration read and explicit revision-based reset support owner handoff. Do not label ready until sign-in, scope, supply/access/pricing and funding have been checked.
notes: Refs #102. Expanded real-router/PostgreSQL handoff test PASSED: fresh company/workspace/owner/password/login/isolation, owner key creation, model discovery, unfunded rejection before dispatch, trusted fixture funding, local Provider response and exactly one customer charge. No merchant checkout or paid upstream traffic; those boundaries remain unqualified. Source: docs/ux/findings.md (UX-04). Latest reconciliation: docs/ux/continuation-2026-10-21.md, All findings reconciled.

Imported disposition: Active, stronger evidence E02: absent global payment does not gate workspace features

Recheck current code/rendering before implementing; migration is not a new reproduction or authorization for product changes.

**P1 · global prerequisite gate · G3/G6, J3/J4/J8 · user-confirmed requirement; current absence observed.**

Observation: the inspected installation exposes workspace features while Settings → Payments reports online top-ups unavailable and payment gateways remain unconfigured (E05, E10). The earlier finding treated this as a local insufficient-funds recovery problem. The user clarified that valid payment setup is a hard global prerequisite: no workspace feature should become available before it is satisfied.

Impact: the product admits users into workspace workflows before a mandatory installation dependency is ready. Adding a funding link or a local warning would leave the global ordering failure intact. An existing balance, credit allowance or personal upstream key is not an implicit exemption from this setup gate.

Required direction: establish one server-authoritative installation payment-readiness gate shared by all workspaces. Until at least one supported payment method has valid, operational configuration, present an installation setup blocker instead of workspace features. Keep administrator payment setup, authentication, sign-out and necessary recovery/help accessible so the installation can be completed. Ordinary users see the blocker and its responsible operator, not merchant credentials or administration controls. Server-managed gateways may retain their supported configuration procedure; an in-dashboard editor is not inherently required.

Readiness must reflect the gateway's required credentials, merchant activation and required integration checks, not merely a saved configuration record. Apply the gate consistently to direct URLs, existing sessions and workspace API operations, not only navigation visibility. Preserve existing data and allow already-started payment callbacks, reconciliation and request settlement to complete. This gate is distinct from each customer's balance and from a single failed or pending payment; those do not by themselves make the whole installation unconfigured.

Verification: with no configured method, invalid/incomplete setup or unknown readiness, workspace entry and operations remain blocked across roles and entry points while an authorized operator can reach the remedy. Completing validated setup unlocks workspace access consistently. Removing or invalidating the last ready method re-establishes the gate without deleting records or abandoning in-flight obligations; another ready method keeps it satisfied. Verify pending/failed individual payments do not incorrectly block all users. Define operational readiness signals and temporary-outage handling before implementation; do not equate one failed transaction with global failure. Actual payment execution and migration remain separately authorized work.

description:
Trigger and outcome: Niu currently models an operator session as belonging to one organization. An organization is the customer and shared billing boundary; it owns workspaces. A person needs one login for multiple independently funded organizations, each with separate members, access and billing. User confirmed that ordinary signed-in users can create multiple organizations and that the user menu should show the current organization and provide a low-prominence switcher.

Scope: Deliver the complete customer journey and agent/API contracts for self-service organization creation, organization identity and settings, organization and workspace membership administration, switching, and organization billing. A personal user may have their own organization; the organization, not each member individually, pays the Niu customer charges in resale mode. Internal-use provider funding remains separate. Organization owner/admin may manage shared billing within authorized scope; only the authorized member-management role may manage members. Workspace-scoped access must not become organization-wide authority. Platform administration and existing installation-only customer provisioning remain distinct.

Existing state and evidence: at source a1b9e0f41, admin_operators and sessions encode one organization and optional workspace; password credentials, profiles and revocation are attached to operators; account-menu selection changes client state and cannot expand session authority. Existing organization settings show identity and workspaces, and financial views are elsewhere. Existing platform customer provisioning niu-lxs.4 is not self-service organization creation. Partial local uncommitted work exists in crates/storage/migrations/0404_organization_identity.sql, crates/storage/src/account_organization_creation.rs, crates/storage/tests/account_organization_creation.rs, crates/storage/src/lib.rs and apps/dashboard/app/shell/AccountMenu.tsx. Treat it as provisional: inspect, revalidate, revise or replace as necessary. Migration 0404 and the storage creation method are not a complete identity system or public endpoint. Existing independent uncommitted dashboard changes must be preserved. niu-2n1 concurrently changes workspace navigation and proposes moving Members; coordinate against current work and keep organization-scope and workspace-scope permissions clear. niu-ayj.40 tracks broader member acceptance.

Design constraints: preserve existing users, sessions where safe, role grants, Provider ownership, workspace references, balances, request and invoice provenance across migration; never merge identities merely because names or email addresses look alike. Identity, organization memberships and selected session scope must be explicit. Creation must atomically establish ownership and independent zero-funded billing and recover safely from uncertain writes without duplicates; create a usable initial workspace or provide a clear supported setup flow. No customer-funded Provider execution may occur without the normal authorized price/funding admission. Changes of organization membership, role, session, password and revocation must be reflected at every authorization point, including transaction-time checks and concurrent operations. Do not broaden workspace members into organization admins or grant installation authority. Account/profile/password lifecycle must work across memberships without exposing or silently transferring another organization's data. Support loss of access, last-owner protection, concurrent changes and safe recovery. Do not invent an email-invitation delivery capability; make existing supported onboarding and its limitations explicit, or implement a complete authorized invitation flow if needed for the journey.

Switching: only show organizations the signed-in account is authorized to access; the server must resolve and authorize the selected membership, not trust a browser selection. The selected workspace, organization settings, usage, billing, requests and agent context must be scoped consistently. Handle no workspace, revoked access, stale tabs, multiple sessions, reload, direct URLs, failed/lost responses and in-flight requests without cross-organization disclosure or charging. Use durable readable organization slugs in browser paths/query scopes as required by AGENTS.md, while preserving existing API identifiers and authorized legacy routes/bookmarks; a slug is never authorization. Maintain customer-only financial serialization, prevent access to platform procurement and other organizations' balances, and retain historical accounting.

UI and documentation: use existing Niu shell and shadcn primitives. In the user menu show current organization and an accessible switcher without a prominent global header control; preserve selected-state checks and account actions. Make organization management discoverable with organization members, workspaces, settings and billing in the appropriate scope; do not label a workspace as an organization or expose internal IDs. Follow actual mature-product references, ux-review and the repo's browser verification gate, including open menu, keyboard, desktop/intermediate/narrow layouts and errors. Update affected English docs, agent onboarding, SDK/contracts and generated API documentation; mark limitations accurately. Keep niu.io as a resale deployment and maintain the separate self-hosted internal-use policy.

description: Trigger: app/lib/route-data.ts maintains a single activeRouteLoad and acquireRouteLoadSignal aborts it whenever authority/endpoint/path changes. React Router runs loaders for all matched routes in parallel; today loaders exist only on leaf routes, so the collision is latent. Impact: future nested loaders fail intermittently with aborted requests; the current design cannot support nested data routes. Limits: not currently triggered because no route branch has two loaders.

description: Trigger: 15 route modules export loader() using loadCriticalRouteEndpoint (app/lib/route-data.ts:136+). On a cold cache it returns {status:'pending', promise} and swallows the promise rejection (void promise.catch), so the router never awaits data and errors never reach the route error boundary. Most pages call useOptionalRouteLoaderData() and ignore the result (customers/page.tsx:32, overview/page.tsx:24); only keys/page.tsx consumes it, and only when status==='ready'. Pages then fetch through useCachedQuery/useEffect, so loader data is unused on cold loads and duplicated on warm loads. description:
Trigger: Creating or rotating an API key when localStorage is unavailable/restricted or after any network interruption.
Impact: KeysView.tsx:181-274,384,412-420 and mutation-recovery.ts:25-88 write a pending record to localStorage before sending POST. If localStorage throws (e.g. Safari Private Browsing), key creation is completely blocked ('The request has not been sent. Browser storage is unavailable...'). If a request is interrupted, all future key creation and rotation in the workspace is locked out behind a 'Review key request' modal ('Confirm what happened before creating or rotating another key'), and if the key was created on the server, line 415/418 forces the user to revoke the newly created key ('Revoke this key before creating a new one') to clear the lock!
Source: apps/dashboard/app/features/keys/mutation-recovery.ts:25-88; apps/dashboard/app/features/keys/components/KeysView.tsx:181-274,349,384,412-420.
notes: CR-05 competitive reset compares server-backed key request reconciliation with browser-storage precondition and pricing component-local attempts. Durable operation discovery should remove storage as a prerequisite while retaining idempotency and secret non-replay. Cross-browser and post-commit lost-response acceptance specified in docs/ux/competitive-reset-2026-11-04.md. This does not authorize discarding existing replay safety.
